title: A cooled fixed-area blackbody keeps less than three percent of pre-dip power in 17 quiet ASASSN-14ko spectra
abstract: We test whether cooling can hide unchanged thermal power in 17 quiet 2023 XMM-Newton spectra of ASASSN-14ko. We add a common blackbody to the published residual model, refit its soft power law, and use a pointwise profile cutoff of Delta W = 2.71. At the reference apparent area, the primary fit permits a temperature up to about 33 eV and 1.6 percent of the reference thermal power. Five settings give 1.6-2.5 percent. Preserving all thermal power needs a temperature below 21-26 eV and an area 165-345 times larger. Removing photons below 0.4 keV weakens the bound most. Separate residual strengths in all 17 spectra have little effect. These are conditional blackbody constraints, not calibrated confidence limits or evidence for cooling. They extend a prior three-spectrum ingress test to the long quiet state. We retain the prior quiet selection and hard spectral floor. Reference uncertainty, variable color correction, physical Compton models and other absorption laws are not included. No orbital stall or dip mechanism is established. Code, URLs, hashes, aggregate profiles and reproduction instructions are supplied. External count spectra remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Pointwise thermal power profiles in 17 quiet spectra. Delta W = 2.71 is relative to the minimum at each fixed temperature, not a joint confidence contour.
